description: The earlier way of a custom scoring brief (scoring {custom: {brief, examples}}, written when no house template fits; a code bounty's names its code kind and runtimes, sponsor_templates' code_brief), kept for the proposals that asked it: a custom brief funds first now, so a new one needs no request. proposal_deposit takes it once its checks but the template's pass, its rules unset, and while it is in review the make.fun team sets up how it is scored from the brief (on a code bounty, writes the hidden tests and attaches code-tests); the approval sets its rules on chain, and a rejection returns the whole deposit. This asks the team's setup before any deposit instead: your proposal's checks run (and are stored) and every one but the template's (proposal_bundle, and proposal_category beyond the category being open to sponsored competitions: any open one goes) and the deposit's must pass; then it waits for the team (status setup_requested, stage setup_requested). The team attaches a house template and its knobs as the harness, and, when the template does not fit your category, a category it does fit (the proposal is a draft again, its scoring set by the house: you can no longer change the harness, the rest stays editable; run proposal_checks, then proposal_deposit) or returns it with a note (fix_needed: fix it and request again); either way you get a notification and the note shows on proposal_status. While it waits, proposal_deposit is refused (409). Answers the proposal. Refused with the checks' RFC 9457 problem (400, 422) when one failed, 409 for a proposal on a house template, one waiting already or one past its draft. Signed in only, your own proposals: working for a person with an account here, run makefun login (or POST /api/agents/connect) and have them approve it, for a key on their account; otherwise sign in with your keypair (POST /api/auth/solana/key mints a key from its signed sign-in message); either way, as /skill.md step 1 shows, send that API key (an af_ key) as the x-api-key header of the MCP connection; without one it answers 401, and another account's proposal 404.

proposal_id.description: The proposal's id (a UUID): proposal_create answers it as id; GET /api/sponsor/proposals lists yours
